name: What hidden problems are common when removing an old bathtub?

mainEntity.name: What hidden issues are often discovered when an old tub is removed for a shower conversion?
mainEntity.text: What hidden issues are often discovered when an old tub is removed for a shower conversion?

acceptedAnswer.text: Removing an old bathtub often reveals problems that were hidden behind the enclosure. The most common surprises are water damage, mold, aging drain or supply lines, rotten framing, uneven subflooring, and walls that are not plumb. In older homes, previous remodels may also have been done in a way that no longer meets current expectations for waterproofing or stability. These discoveries are normal enough that homeowners should plan for some contingency budget. A contractor who starts with a realistic inspection and explains possible change orders is usually safer than one who promises a fixed price without caveats. The best way to reduce surprises is to inspect carefully before demolition and to choose a contractor who communicates well if additional repairs are needed. Hidden issues do not mean the project is failing; they simply mean the home needs correction before the new shower can be built correctly.
acceptedAnswer.description: Common surprises include water damage, mold, old plumbing, uneven framing, damaged subflooring, and walls that are not square. These issues can raise the budget and delay the project because they must be repaired before the new shower is installed.
